summary: The agency acknowledged it had not yet reached a final decision on the classification issue and stated the final EIS would consider environmental and resource impacts from a range of fuel economy standard levels and alternative classification decisions, ultimately providing for two classes of nonpassenger automobiles (recreational-type with off-road capability and all others).
text: Obviously, the agency has not had time to reach a final decision on either of these issues. Therefore, the final environmental impact statement will consider the environmental and resource impacts that will result from a range of levels of fuel economy standards, and from alternative decisions on the classification issue. This approach will enable both the Administrator and the public to see the relative environmental impacts resulting from the choice of one course of action over alternative choices.
